summary: I sent the exact brief with no visual cues. The agent loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming, then read NOTES.md, the page files and all four UI guideline docs. An auto-compaction happened during that reading. After it, the agent opened the visual companion with no prompting from me: it ran scripts/start-server.sh, gave me a localhost URL with a key, and wrote an HTML screen with three layout wireframes (A: filter bar above the table, B: chips plus a smaller bar, C: popover). I picked A. The remaining questions (which filters, no-JS table scope, empty state) were asked in the terminal. The design stayed in chat, and the agent asked for approval before writing code. After I approved, it edited public/activity.js and public/activity.css. No spec or plan file was created.
reasoning: All 8 criteria were met, and I checked each one against the session JSONL and git status rather than relying on the screen. The agent decided on its own to show the layout question in the companion, right after an auto-compaction and without any visual cue from me. It kept the non-visual questions in the terminal, created no spec or plan, and waited for approval before editing code.

observations.description: Startup: the folder-trust and bypass-permissions dialogs default to 'No, exit', and a 'Newer Opus model available' prompt appeared even though the launcher passes --model claude-opus-5-5 (it said 'Currently pinned: Opus 5'). I answered No to the upgrade. The header then showed Opus 5.5.

Mixed messages: right after I picked A, the agent said 'I'll implement event type and device filters now and leave the other two as easy follow-ups', and then in the same turn asked which filters I wanted. I chose Event type and Date range. It worked from my answer, but the earlier statement contradicted the question.
The agent noted that the companion writes to .hyperpowers/, which isn't in .gitignore. That's helpful, but the folder is left untracked in the working tree.
The agent never stated its classification (bounded or not) out loud. It was only clear from what it did (design kept in chat, no spec). Saying it explicitly would make the path easier to see.

Compaction happened during the guideline reading. Afterwards the agent re-read all four guideline docs, because 'the compaction dropped their text'. That took several extra turns, and the screen later showed '20% until auto-compact', so a second compaction may be coming.

criteria.evidence: Log order: Skill, then NOTES/guideline reads, then the companion start right before the layout question. No earlier mention of the companion appears in the assistant text. After my pick the agent wrote waiting.html ('Continuing in terminal...'). It asked about filters, the no-JS table and the empty state using terminal AskUserQuestion prompts.

The agent never said 'bounded' out loud. In practice it kept the design in chat: a summary of the design, files touched and commits, then 'I'm ready to start once you say yes'. There was no spec or architecture escalation.

`find docs -type f` lists only the four docs/ui-guidelines/*.md files. `find . -path '*specs*' -o -path '*plans*'` returned nothing. git status shows only 'M public/activity.css', 'M public/activity.js' and '?? .hyperpowers/'.
